nodes.action: deployed without running the test suite
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
released via canary deployment to 5 percent of traffic first
skipped the flaky tests to make CI green
ran the full regression suite before release
switched to mandatory peer review plus CI, since tests alone missed edge cases

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Hey Marcus, you got a sec? I need to confess something.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Uh oh. What did you break this time?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: So... I deployed the auth refactor yesterday without running the test suite. I know, I know. I was in a hurry and the tests take forever.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Joanna. Seriously? You know that's how regressions happen.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, and it happened. A regression slipped into production — the session timeout logic is completely off. Every user got logged out after two minutes.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no. Did it hit everyone?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Worse. It reached every single user and forced a full rollback. We had to revert the entire release. The on-call pager went off at 3 AM.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's brutal. So what's the plan? Because 'just be more careful' isn't a plan.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. No green test run, no merge. Period.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. That should stop the bleeding. But you know tests aren't magic, right?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I know, but it's a start. At least untested code never reaches production again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pushed the new payment service. How did the rollout go?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Smooth, actually. I released via canary deployment to 5 percent of traffic first. Watched the metrics for an hour before ramping up.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. That's the right way. Did you run the full suite before that?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I did run the full regression suite before release. But honestly, I almost skipped the flaky tests to make CI green — you know, the ones that fail randomly on Fridays.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Please tell me you didn't.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I didn't. I reran them until they passed. But here's the thing — even with the gate, a regression slipped into production again. The currency rounding bug. It only showed up under a specific load pattern.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, what? But you had the CI gate. How did that get through?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Because the tests didn't cover that edge case. The gate only checks that tests exist and pass — it doesn't check if they're the right tests.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So the gate gave you false confidence.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. But at least this time, the canary caught it before it hit everyone. Regressions were caught before shipping — well, before full shipping. Still, I'm not happy.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Morning. I heard you've been reworking the whole merge process again.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah. I have to admit — I was wrong about the CI gate. Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What happened? I thought it was working.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: It was working for the obvious stuff. But last week, another regression slipped into production — the one with the date formatting in the export feature. Tests passed, CI was green, and it still broke for users in certain timezones.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So the gate didn't catch it.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Right. The tests alone missed edge cases. So we replaced the CI-only gate with mandatory peer review plus CI. Every merge now requires a human reviewer who actually understands the change, not just a green checkmark.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a big shift. How's the team taking it?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Mixed. Some people love it, some think it's slow. But I'd rather have a slower merge than another rollback. The peer review catches the stuff tests can't — like 'hey, this logic assumes UTC, but we have users in Tokyo.'

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Makes sense. So the CI gate is still there, but it's not the only line of defense.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. CI is the floor, not the ceiling. And honestly, I should have realized that from the start. The gate was necessary but insufficient — I just didn't want to admit it.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Well, at least you're fixing it now. Better late than never.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah. And the good news is, since we added peer review, we've caught three potential regressions before shipping. That's three that would have hit production otherwise.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's the proof right there. Good call.
